newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rohm to begin mass production of FRAM in FY97/98.
newsitem.headline: Rohm to begin mass production of FRAM in FY97/98.

text.p: Rohm Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it would start mass-producing ferroelectric random-access memory (FRAM) chips as early as fiscal 1997/98, which starts next April 1.
FRAM chips can retain memory without electricity and the memory can be rewritten up to one trillion times.
The Kyoto-based firm plans to start producing 1,000 six-inch wafers per month in September and boost production to 10,000 in the next fiscal year.
FRAM chips can store 14 kilobits, 16 kilobits and 64 kilobits of memory.
The chip's possible applications include train passes, which can be automatically read by holding it up to a sensor, a company spokesman said.
Rohm would be the first Japanese firm to mass produce FRAM chips, the spokesman said.
